source_text: ወተስእሉኒ፡ ከመ፡ እጽሐፍ፡ ሎሙ፡ *ትዝካረ፡ ስእለት፡ ከመ፡ ይኩኖሙ፡ ኅድገተ፡ ወ*ከመ፡ አነ፡ አዕርግ፡ ትዝካረ፡ ስእለቶሙ፡ ቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ ሰማይ።

translation.text: And they asked me to write for them a record of their petition, so that they might receive forgiveness, and so that I might bring the record of their petition up before the Lord of heaven.[a]

footnotes.text: Literally, a memorial of petition. Charles 1906 stars the memorial wording and the second connective; the complete printed clause specifies bringing their petition before the Lord of heaven. The earlier POB wording was cut off by the OCR page window, not by a manuscript lacuna.

source_text: እስመ፡ *እሙንቱሰ፡ ኢይክሉ፡ እምይእዜ፡ ተናግሮ፡ ወኢያነስኡ፡ አዕይንቲሆሙ፡ ውስተ፡ ሰማይ፡ እምኃፍረት፡ አበሳሆሙ፡ ዘተኰነኑ።

translation.text: For they could no longer speak or lift their eyes to heaven, because of the shame of their sins for which they had been condemned.[a]

footnotes.text: Charles 1906 stars the pronoun introducing the explanation. The main text follows his selected wording without inserting an unstated recipient of the speech.

source_text: አሜሃ፡ ጸሐፍኩ፡ ትዝካረ፡ ስእለቶሙ፡ ወአስተብቍዖተ፡ በእንተ፡ መንፈሶሙ፡ ወ*ለለአሐዱ፡ ምግባሮሙ፡ ወበእንተ፡ ዘይስእሉ፡ ከመ፡ ይኩኖሙ፡ ስርየተ፡ ወአስተ።

translation.text: Then I wrote a record of their petition and supplication concerning their spirits and the deeds of each one, and concerning their request that forgiveness and an extension be granted to them.[a][b]

footnotes.text: The printed final noun, አስተ, is provisionally rendered “extension” or “prolongation.” Apparatus note 13 reports that witness y adds “days” and puts the surrounding terms in the nominative. The selected main text does not include “days.”
Charles 1906 stars the distributive expression rendered “each one.” The main text retains the deeds of each one, not merely a collective summary.

source_text: ወሐዊርየ፡ ነበርኩ፡ ዲበ፡ ማያተ፡ *ዳን፡ በዳን፡ እንዘ፡ ይእቲ፡ እምየማነ፡ ዐረብ፡ አርሞን፡ ወአነብብ፡ ትዝካረ፡ ስእለቶሙ፡ እስከ፡ ደቀስኩ።

translation.text: And I went and sat by the waters of Dan, in Dan, which lies southwest of Armon,[a] and read the record of their petition[b] until I fell asleep.

footnotes.text: The selected text spells the mountain name አርሞን, Armon. Its compressed directional wording combines right/south and west; “southwest” is provisional. The first “Dan” is a starred selected reading, and apparatus note 15 lists a variant. No certain modern geographical identification is asserted.

source_text: ወናሁ፡ ሕልም፡ መጽአኒ፡ ወራእያት፡ ዲቤየ፡ ወደቁ፡ ወርኢኩ፡ ራእያተ፡ መቅሠፍት፡ (ወመጽአ፡ ቃል፡ እንዘ፡ ይብል፡) እንግር፡ ለውሉደ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወእዝልፎሙ።

translation.text: And behold, a dream came to me, and visions fell upon me. I saw visions of punishment, and a word came[a] saying that I should tell the children of heaven and rebuke them.

footnotes.text: Charles 1906 places “and a word came, saying” in parentheses. His apparatus note 27 explicitly identifies this as an editorial restoration in accordance with Greek. It is retained as part of the selected critical edition, not claimed as directly preserved wording in all Ethiopic manuscripts.

source_text: ወነቂሕየ፡ መጻእኩ፡ ኀቤሆሙ፡ ወኵሎሙ፡ ጉቡኣን፡ ይነብሩ፡ እንዘ፡ ይላሕዉ፡ በ*አበልስያኤል፡ ዘሀለወት፡ ማእከለ፡ ሊባኖስ፡ ወ*ሴኒሴር፡ እንዘ፡ ግልቡባን፡ ገጾሙ።

translation.text: And when I awoke, I came to them, and they were all sitting together, weeping at Abälsyael, which is between Lebanon and Seniser, with their faces covered.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected printed spellings are አበልስያኤል, here rendered Abälsyael, and ሴኒሴር, Seniser. Both are starred; apparatus notes 32–33 list variant spellings. These are critical-edition selections, not fresh manuscript testimony or certain modern geographical identifications.

source_text: ወተናገርኩ፡ ቅድሜሆሙ፡ ኵሎ፡ ራእያተ፡ ዘርኢኩ፡ በንዋም፡ ወወጠንኩ፡ እትናገር፡ ውእተ፡ ቃላተ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ወእዝልፍ፡ ለትጉሃነ፡ ሰማይ።

translation.text: And I recounted before them all the visions I had seen while asleep, and I began to speak those words of righteousness and to rebuke the Watchers of heaven.
